question: Which was the first statute in the modern State of Israel to explicitly introduce the concept of "good faith"? (Do not append "the" or the statute's year to the answer.)

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Contracts Law
I believe the Contracts (General Part) Law, 1973, was the earliest modern Israeli statute to codify the duty of good faith, drawing directly from continental civil-law traditions and applying it as a general principle across contractual relations. Earlier legislation like the Sale Law focused more narrowly on specific transactions without explicitly framing good faith as a standalone obligation.
